title: Choose QueueUp's visual world
question: The roll assigned The Ballpark Scoreboard. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Ballpark Scoreboard
options.lineage: hand-slotted steel scoreboards and incandescent bulb boards at old ballparks
options.thesis: Every event is a live game: the board shows the count, and the count is never wrong.
options.viewport: A full-width scoreboard: QUEUEUP across the header, a bulb-matrix counter dropping SEATS LEFT from 1 as 100 lit request bulbs fight for it, the final reading 1 IN, 99 OUT, then two plate buttons: HOST AN EVENT and FIND AN EVENT.
options.risk: Can read as sports-themed novelty if the board decorates instead of carrying real counts.

raised.raise: State is illumination: lit, dim, or dark bulbs carry every status, with no colored badges anywhere.
Flat paint only, zero shadows or gradients; each section is anchored by one emblematic board object.
The committed outcome renders solid while the alternatives render dashed (the winning request lit, the 99 losers outlined).
How it works is told by four oversized step numerals with almost no words.
Every element sits on one measured cell module, the board's slot grid, with nothing placed by eye.
Total ink discipline: exactly the board's four paints (green, plate white, bulb amber, out red) and nothing else.

options.label: Photo Finish
options.lineage: race-timing photo-finish strips and printed results sheets
options.thesis: A hundred hands reach for one seat; the strip shows exactly who crossed first, by milliseconds.
options.viewport: A stretched slit-scan strip of 100 requests streaming past a red finish line, one crossing first; a printed results table beside it reads 1 RESERVED, 99 SOLD OUT with ms timings.
options.risk: It topped my list, and it lands close to the familiar editorial-paper look, with the most drama on desktop.

options.label: Oscilloscope Bench
options.lineage: CRT oscilloscope on a signal bench
options.thesis: The race as a measured signal: 100 traces triggered, one locks still.
options.viewport: A graticule with 100 request traces converging and one locking on trigger.
options.case: Engineers identify with it, but attendees and organizers don't; it loses both axes for an audience of everyone.
options.risk: Lands in the near-black, one-neon rut.
options.kept: Every element measured against one grid module.

options.label: Signboard Alley
options.thesis: Events as a glowing vertical index of nights out.
options.viewport: A spine of lit signs, one per event, reflected below.
options.case: Fits attendees, but has nothing that explains no-oversell or the door.
options.risk: Reads as a nightlife guide, not a ticketing system.

options.label: Push Pin Poster
options.thesis: Every event as a flat-color illustrated poster.
options.viewport: One silhouette poster with event vignettes orbiting it.
options.case: Charming for attendees, but it hides the mechanism.
options.risk: Illustration-heavy; needs artwork we don't have.

options.label: Sewing Pattern
options.thesis: Ticket tiers as graded size lines on tissue.
options.viewport: Nested dashed lines with the chosen one drawn solid.

options.label: Build Instructions
options.thesis: Hosting an event as numbered assembly steps.
options.viewport: Step 1 to 4 spreads with pieces dropping onto studs.
options.case: Clear process for organizers, but it misses the live race.
options.risk: Toy register undercuts trust in payments.
options.kept: Oversized step numerals do the teaching.

options.label: Risograph System
options.thesis: Event pages as misregistered gig prints.
options.viewport: Overprinted ink shapes with the product name in one spot color.
options.case: Gig-culture fit, but no mechanism and a well-worn look.
options.kept: A strict limit on the number of inks.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS ticketing landing page, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and subhead on the left, a product screenshot on the right, two buttons, then feature rows.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other ticketing site by design.
